findings.claim: ADR-0002 decision 2 says 'No retry loop' for SQLite writes (BEGIN IMMEDIATE only, timeout:5000, no withRetry). This re-breaks a fix v1 already made and documented as correct.
findings.evidence: ARCHAEOLOGY: INTRODUCED_BY 065799f8 'fix(db-base): rollback v1.0.128 lockfile + EXCLUSIVE pragma (v1.0.130 slice 2)', 2026-05-14, cm-main repo. ORIGINAL_INTENT (commit message, quoted): 'Process-identity invariants belong in the process layer (sibling-mcp), not the DB layer. WAL + busy_timeout + withRetry(SQLITE_BUSY) is the right defense for multi-writer SQLite.' The diff removes the single-writer lockfile (introduced in e24934f6 / 5e652e52 for #560) and keeps `withRetry` (src/db-base.ts:432, 604-605) plus `busy_timeout` (src/db-base.ts:266-308) as the surviving, endorsed defense. git log -S 'checkpoint' and git log --oneline on db-base.ts show the single-writer-lockfile line (#560) was tried and explicitly rejected in favor of WAL+busy_timeout+withRetry, which is still present on origin/main @ 5869f4fa. TECH-SPEC's own cited source (verify-single-db.md, quoted in ADR-0002 Context) says the #985 CPU spin came from 'v1's own withRetry busy loop (src/db-base.ts:446)', and treats that as the reason to delete retries — but that conflates a buggy retry loop (unbounded busy-spin) with the retry mechanism itself; the rollback commit says the fix for #985-class issues is the process layer, not removing withRetry, and v1 kept withRetry after the #985 fix.
findings.fix: ADR-0002 should keep a bounded withRetry (the delays:[100,500,2000] pattern already in db-base.ts) around BEGIN IMMEDIATE, not drop retries outright. If the owner's measured spike (verify-single-db.md, 8 writers/0 busy errors) is judged sufficient to go retry-less, ADR-0002 must say explicitly why it diverges from the 065799f8 finding and from the still-present v1 withRetry, citing the #985 fix as 'loop was unbounded', not 'retry is unnecessary'. SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: any no-retry design must guarantee the lockfile/EXCLUSIVE-pragma path from #560 is not silently reintroduced through ADR-0002's single-DB-per-project model, since that path was tried and reverted for breaking multi-window UX.

findings.claim: TECH-SPEC §2b and the ADR list (0001-0017) describe M0-relevant decisions (single DB, enforcement rewrite, compaction) but the document has no explicit module boundary / dependency diagram for M0 (which module owns db-base vs adapters vs enforcement vs prompt), despite ADR-0002 introducing a schema with 4 tables (events, sources, chunks FTS5, meta) that multiple ADRs (0008 enforcement, 0009 compaction, 0016 subagent protection) all read/write.
findings.evidence: Searched TECH-SPEC.md sections 0-3 (the only parts read in this pass): no 'module', 'boundary', or dependency-graph section exists before §3. ADR-0002 defines the DB schema; ADR-0008 (enforcement+cap) and ADR-0016 (subagent context protection) both depend on it per DECISIONS-r3.md Q1/Q2, but no doc states which module is authoritative for writing `meta` vs `events` or who owns migration between ADR-0002's schema version and future changes.
findings.fix: Add an M0 module-ownership table to TECH-SPEC (or a new ADR) naming one module per table/responsibility (db-base, enforcement, prompt-instructions, adapters) before implementation starts, so ADR-0008/0009/0016's shared dependence on ADR-0002's schema has one clear owner for schema changes.
